newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends sharply lower, Dec breaks support.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends sharply lower, Dec breaks support.

text.p: NYCE cotton ended weaker in technically driven trade that accelerated once benchmark December fell through its downside target of 76.10 cents a lb, trading sources said.
The most-active month closed down 0.89 cent at 75.80 cents after trading from 76.60 to 75.61 cents. The rest settled 0.92 to 0.65 lower.
An estimated 10,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Wednesday's official tally of 5,747 lots.
Traders said the failure to pierce the recent high of 77.65 cents in December attraced speculative selling ahead of the long weekend.
NYCE will be closed Friday for Independence Day.
December delivery ran into stops around 76.00 cents and slid to a session nadir of 75.61 cents, its lowest since 75.40 cents on June 24.
Traders pegged nearby support at 75.40 cents followed by 75.00 cents for December cotton.

USDA's weekly export and sales report put some fundamental pressure on prices. USDA said new sales of upland cotton reached 63,200 480-lb bales for the 1997/98 crop, and 41,000 bales for the current season in the week ended June 26.

"We continue to run a touch behind (on weekly exports)," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said. The U.S. is more likely to export 7.0 million bales rather than the 7.1 million bales the USDA has forecast for the 1996/97 marketing year, she added.
